design:
Decisions taken during the mock (operator, 2026-11-12):
- Today's centred dialog with blur, header and Story (traces and conversation links) stays. The side sheet and the two-column dialog were rejected: the operator said today's looks better and wants fewer changes.
- The real TaskStory component is trimmed in place; no parallel timeline component (its class names broke the real story).
- Today's Details content is split into Work (requirements with evidence state, criteria, latest checks, Earlier runs) and a reworked Details (description, waits-on/needed-by, notes, facts, history, escalation). Today's controls are kept inside it.
- Work reads evidence state from the document's coverage, not the requirement's lifecycle field (that field is active/retired).
- The mock lives at hub/ui/mock#task-redesign. The dialog work (story trim, Work, Details) is in the real components on master since 59333db; the new TaskCard, StageThread and taskStageVisual exist but only the mock uses them.
- Style classes use the aw-tview prefix; aw-sheet clashes with story.css's fixed right-hand panel. Buttons use the app's Button component with data-slot, because the global button style otherwise hides them.
- The acceptance drive is a browser drive script under scripts/drive, outside the test suite, so it can be written and failing first without failing the project's checks. Its task is approved on a drive_baseline showing each check reached and failing at its own assertion; the final task runs it green.

open_questions.question: Which story entries are never folded? Resolved 2026-11-12: created, finished building, approved, sent back, landed or did not land, closed, any failure, anything waiting on the operator, and answered questions.
On narrow cards, does waits-on beat time at stage? Resolved 2026-11-12: yes.

problem: Cards and especially the task story (TaskStory.tsx, sentences such as '<agent> is working') carry too much text, so it is hard to understand what is in a task. The operator asked for a redesign based on best UI/UX practice, with animation and finish, in AgentWeave's visual identity (brand/ in the repository is the identity kit).

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-20: mocks are the real components fed fixtures, so applying one is wiring rather than redrawing. Approved 2026-11-12.
requirements.statement: The redesign is shown first as a mock built from the real board, card, dialog and story components fed fixtures. The mock covers every stage from slice glance and every close from slice loose-tasks. Nothing is wired to live data until the operator approves the mock.

A card shows only: its title; its stage as a glyph and a word; time at stage; the waits-on line when waiting; builder and reviewer; its spec's short tag; a failing-checks marker; and priority only when critical.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-12: what a card is stuck on is actionable, how long it has been stuck is not.
requirements.statement: Apart from its title, no card shows more than two lines of text at the board's default width. When the waits-on line and time at stage do not both fit, waits-on is kept and time at stage gives way; when names are long, the builder's name is cut before the reviewer's.
Description, branch, commits, requirements and acceptance criteria appear in the opened task and never on the card.
A task whose latest checks failed shows, before review, a marker on its card naming how many checks failed. Opening the task lists them in its Work view.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-12: answered questions record decisions, which is what is looked for later.
requirements.statement: The Story keeps every link it has today (traces, conversations) and shows each entry as a glyph, a label of at most six words, the actor and the time. Runs of four or more consecutive routine entries fold into one entry that opens. These are never folded: created, finished building, approved, sent back, landed or did not land, closed, any failure, anything waiting on the operator, and questions the operator answered. Any entry can be expanded to its full text.

The opened task has a Work view listing the requirements it serves, each with its evidence state read from the document's coverage, the requirement's acceptance criteria, and the latest checks with their outcome. An Earlier runs control shows the checks of previous runs.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-12: fewer changes; dropping today's controls was rejected.
requirements.statement: The opened task's Details view shows description, waits-on and needed-by tasks, notes, facts, history and escalation, and keeps every control today's Details offers. Facts never repeat their label in their value (no 'Built by: built by Developer').
A card changing stage animates the change, finishing within 300 ms. With reduced motion requested by the system, no animation plays and the change still shows.
Colours, type and glyphs come from AgentWeave's identity kit, in both light and dark themes.
No stage or marker is conveyed by colour alone. All card and story text meets WCAG AA contrast in both themes.

The Hub data the card needs for its failing-checks count
non_goals: What a card's stage facts are and how they are computed (slices glance, loose-tasks and finding)
Replacing the centred dialog with a side sheet

summary: Cards and the opened task are redesigned around visual state instead of prose. The card shows a stage line, a people line and a stage thread. Today's centred dialog stays, with a trimmed Story, a new Work view (requirements with evidence state, criteria, latest checks) and a reworked Details view. The mock was approved by the operator on 2026-11-12; this change wires it to live data.
